12/12.07.2024
1.
Learned counsel for the parties are present.

2. This writ petition has been filed for the following reliefs:
"For issuance of appropriate writ/writs, order/orders, direction/directions commanding upon the respondents to immediately and forthwith to pay/release to the petitioners, the a) Compensation amount in lieu of acquisition of their house.

Bashudeo Sahu S/O Late Prayag Sahu vs State Of Jharkhand Through The Deputy ... on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192948950/
1 b) Payment of compensation as per the Right To Fair Compensation And Transparency In Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation And Resettlement Act, 2013.
c) Interest @ 18% p.a. from the date of acquisition till date of payment.
d) Costs of the case And for issuance of any other appropriate writ, order, direction as Your Lordships may deem fit and proper for doing conscionable Justice to the petitioner."
3. The learned counsel for the respondents have preferred to the counter affidavit dated 05.07.2019 and in particular has referred to Paragraphs 10 and 16, which reads as follows:
" 10.
That it is humbly stated and submitted that enhance rate of the award for the construction of the structure made on the acquired land of Mouza - Harchanda.

P.S.-
Ormanjhi, Khata No. 04, Plot No. 54, area 0.6 decimal has not been paid to the petitioner as yet because Sri Baijnath Prasad Gupta the younger brother of the petitioner has made an objection the he is also entitle to payment of compensation for construction of structure made on the said acquired land.

16. That in view of the submission made herein above it is quite clear that the compensation for construction of structure for the acquired land in question has not been paid to the petitioner as his younger brother Sri Baijnath Prasad Gupta has made an objection for payment of compensation which is pending in the court of the District Land Acquisition Officer, Ranchi."

4. The learned counsel for the respondents has referred to an order passed by this Court in W.P. (C)
5082 of 2017 passed on 19.07.2023 and has submitted that in case of dispute between two brothers with regard to entitlement of the compensation amount the matter has to be determined through a civil court who has to adjudicate the matter in terms of Section 3-H (4) of National Highways Act,
1956.
He refers to Paragraph 12 of the aforesaid Act of 1956 .
5. No rejoinder to the counter affidavit has been filed.

6. After hearing the learned counsel for the respondents, this Court finds that as per the counter affidavit, there is a dispute between the petitioner and his younger brother Sri. Baijnath Prasad Gupta with regard to payment of enhanced compensation.
Sri Baijnath Prasad Gupta has not been made a party in the present proceeding.

7. In W.P.(C) No. 5082 of 2017, it has been observed in paragraph 12 that in case of any dispute regarding apportionment of compensation amount the matter has to be referred to the civil court for adjudication in terms of Section 3H of National Highway Act, 1956.

The said paragraph is quoted as under:
Bashudeo Sahu S/O Late Prayag Sahu vs State Of Jharkhand Through The Deputy ... on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192948950/
2 "12.

entities.text: Bashudeo Sahu S/O Late Prayag Sahu vs State Of Jharkhand Through The Deputy ... on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court finds that as per the provisions of Section 3H of National Highway Act, 1956, the amount of determined compensation is to be deposited by the Central Government and if there is any dispute regarding apportionment of the amount, the matter is to be referred to the principal court of original jurisdiction in terms of section 3H (4).

In the judgment passed by this Court in W.P.(C) No.1832 of 2017 (supra), this Court has held that even title dispute in connection with the acquired property is to be referred to the civil court for adjudication in terms of Section 3H of National Highway Act, 1956."

8. It appears that there is a dispute of title between two brothers and in such circumstances,
appropriate decision is required to be taken by the Authority in terms of section 3-H (4) of the aforesaid Act of 1956 if not already taken.
The counter affidavit was filed way back in 2019 stating that the matter was pending in the court of District Land Acquisition Officer, Ranchi.
9. In view of the aforesaid dispute no relief as prayed for by the petitioner in this writ petition can be granted.

However, liberty is reserved with the petitioner to approach the respondent No. 3 within a periods of 10 weeks from today along with a copy of the writ records, a copy of this order and supporting documents.

10. The respondent No.3 is directed to take appropriate steps in accordance with law in terms of section 3-H (4) of the National Highways Act, 1956 read with order passed by this Court in W.P.(C)
No. 5082 of 2017 dated 19.07.2023.
11.
This writ petition is accordingly disposed of.
12. Pending I.A., if any, is closed.

(Anubha Rawat Choudhary, J.) Rakesh Bashudeo Sahu S/O Late Prayag Sahu vs State Of Jharkhand Through The Deputy ... on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192948950/
